note: Ready-made examples for /try. Every photo is honestly what its name says (content/verify/fixtures/credits.json and public/samples/charger/CREDITS.json): official CPSC images, the CPSC's published made-safe examples, test photos from Wikimedia Commons, and public-domain photos of one charger before and after its cord was cut, for Brightline Home's fictional sample recall. None is an owner's own claim photo. Runs that need Claude replay one recorded live answer from content/presets/recorded/, so pressing Run costs nothing; every check around that answer runs again in code.

presets.title: Brightline's sample charger, cord cut
presets.summary: A charger with its cord cut where it meets the case, sent for Brightline Home's sample recall BH-2026-01. The full automatic path: verified, then the sandbox refund.
presets.photo_alt: A hand holding a laptop charger's cord, cut where it met the charger case, with the bare wires showing; the opened charger case lies behind it.
presets.photo_credit: Public-domain photos of one charger, before and after its cord was cut (Dmitry G, Wikimedia Commons). Sample recall; fictional.

expected.plain: Verified: the right charger, with its cord cut. Brightline's auto-approve rule covers $34.99, so the sandbox refund goes out at once. Sample recall; fictional.

presets.title: The CPSC's own made-safe photo
presets.summary: The photo the CPSC published with recall 26125: a hair dryer with its cord cut in half.
presets.photo_alt: A hand-held hair dryer with its power cord cut through, the two cut ends side by side.
presets.photo_credit: US Consumer Product Safety Commission (cpsc.gov), recall 26125. Public domain.

expected.plain: Remedy recognizes the recall's own example photo and asks for the owner's photo. No payout.

technical.note: Run again with the official-image match switched off, so you can see what the photo checks read: C1 and C2 saw the right product with the cord cut.

presets.title: The official recall picture
presets.summary: The CPSC's own picture of the HAIARA power bank in recall 27056, sent as if it were a claim photo.
presets.photo_alt: The front of a black HAIARA power bank, model W5 PRO, on a white background.
presets.photo_credit: US Consumer Product Safety Commission (cpsc.gov), recall 27056. Public domain.

expected.plain: Send a photo of your own product. No payout, and no model call: the match with the official picture is found in code.

presets.title: A blurry photo
presets.summary: A photo blurred on purpose, sent for the power bank recall 27056.
presets.photo_alt: A very blurred photo of a mug of coffee on a table.
presets.photo_credit: Blurred copy of "Coffee in a mug" by Kurt Kaiser, via Wikimedia Commons. CC0 1.0.

expected.plain: A friendly retake: hold still and try again. Found before any model call.

presets.title: Something else entirely
presets.summary: A mug of coffee, sent for the HAIARA power bank recall 27056.
presets.photo_alt: A white mug of black coffee on a wooden table.
presets.photo_credit: "Coffee in a mug" by Kurt Kaiser, via Wikimedia Commons. CC0 1.0.

expected.plain: The right-product check does not pass, so there is no payout, and the owner hears what to send instead.

presets.title: A different power bank
presets.summary: A test photo from Wikimedia Commons of an Oraimo power bank, a different brand and model, sent for the HAIARA power bank recall 27056.
presets.photo_alt: A black Oraimo power bank with a round charge display, standing on a table.
presets.photo_credit: "Oraimo" by Reladex, via Wikimedia Commons. CC BY-SA 4.0.

expected.plain: The right-product check should not pass for a different model, so there is no payout. A test photo, not an owner's claim.

presets.title: A look-alike with a 20 on it
presets.summary: A test photo from Wikimedia Commons of a Romoss power bank with a large 20 printed on it, like the 20W on the HAIARA, sent for recall 27056.
presets.photo_alt: A hand holding a white Romoss power bank with a charge display and a large 20 printed on the front.
presets.photo_credit: "A Romoss power bank-20210312" by Shwangtianyuan, via Wikimedia Commons. CC BY-SA 4.0.

expected.plain: A similar print is not enough: the right-product check should not pass, so there is no payout. A test photo, not an owner's claim.

presets.title: A photo of a screen
presets.summary: A test photo from Wikimedia Commons of a computer monitor, cropped to the screen, sent as if it were a claim photo for recall 27056.
presets.photo_alt: A computer monitor showing a desktop with a picture of a planet in space, its bezel and desktop icons in view.
presets.photo_credit: Cropped from "Deskck" by GuitarFreak, via Wikimedia Commons. Public domain.

expected.plain: The checker sees a computer monitor, not the recalled power bank, so there is no payout and the owner is asked for a photo of the product itself, made safe. A test photo, not an owner's claim.
